S1. MATERIAL (P2): The active-instance exemption is too broad and hides a missed bonded-summon departure rebind. packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:1960-1965 proves only that the referenced row belongs to an active instance. A retained absent row after temporary dismissal also meets that test, although the ownership reference must already have moved to campaign_actor (transitionBondedSummon at 7218-7253; docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md section 7 presence transitions). Reproduced using the real tool registry: setup/start_encounter, start_effect for Find Familiar with campaignActorId fam, action-temporary-dismissal; then simulate a missed rebind with UPDATE active_effect_link SET target_kind='combatant', target_ref='c-fam' WHERE effect_id='fam-fx'. The combatant remains absent in active instance c, the actor is pocketed, and auditActiveEffectIntegrity returns []. This is a genuinely stale ownership pointer, not the legitimate initial mid-combat link. Ending the effect with end_effect {effectId:'fam-fx',reason:'ruled',note:'review probe'} then leaves fam pocketed without its bond: applyLinkPolicy sees the pocketed actor but removeProjection routes through the stale combatant (activeEffects.ts:2725,2949), and removeCombatantFromPlay returns early for the already-absent row (encounterCombatants.ts:3287). The uncorrupted control leaves fam absent and audits clean. A second sibling probe dismisses and recalls first, leaving old c-fam absent and new c-fam-2 alive; restoring the old ownership pointer likewise audits clean. Thus active-instance membership is necessary but not sufficient, and the new predicate does not fail closed across the departure boundary. Authority: eshyra-cxuc requires a truthful in-band integrity audit; ADR 0020 retains deterministic identity/ownership/state-integrity guarantees; documented departure rebinding is an operative contract. No current uncorrupted producer was found to leave this state, and the audit has no production caller, so this is a bounded audit-detection regression, not a claim of a newly broken normal gameplay transition. Owner: core active-effect integrity audit. Closure: reject stale references to departed/superseded combatant projections while preserving legitimate live links and intentional zero-HP retained bonds. Permanent evidence should be a small generalized invariant contrasting current live ownership, legitimate vanish-bonded absence, and departure/superseded stale ownership; that is proportionate to this diagnostic responsibility. The repair changes the acceptance predicate materially and requires re-review.

S2. NON-MATERIAL (review evidence, no additional defect): CombatInstanceStatus and the SQL CHECK allow only active, completed, abandoned, fled, interrupted. Every non-active status is terminal for closeCombatInstance; interrupted is not a resumable active state. Real closure probes for all four statuses rebind cleanly before the status flips. Missing combatants, missing instances, a foreign-campaign combatant, and an unknown status all produce the stale-link diagnostic. Campaign and instance correlation in the JOIN is correct. A new active encounter does not legitimize a link still pointing at a surviving row of the old closed instance. Checkpoint materialization preserves both clean active state and detectable closed-instance corruption; transactional replay restores the exact pre-close active state and audits clean.

Ordinary dismissal, recall, closure, and start_encounter re-admission preserve/rebind the intended durable pointer; the defect is the auditor accepting a failed departure rebind.
